chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said:
The inheritance of the son of the fornicator is for his relatives from his mother's side, in the manner of the inheritance of the son of the mu'alanah (one who undergoes li'an).

This is a suspended narration (mawquf) which Yunus did not attribute to any of the Imams (peace be upon them). It is possible that this was his own choice, not based on transmission from an Imam, but based on a type of consideration. And this is its ruling: it is not objected to by the many narrations that we have presented previously.

key_terms.ابْنِ الْمُلاَعَنَةِ: Son of the mu'alanah (one who undergoes li'an)

ai.seo_question: How does inheritance work for the son of the fornicator according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that the son of the fornicator (walad al-zina) inherits from his maternal kin according to the same principles applied to the son of the mu'alanah (those of the mubahala incident). The scholar notes that Yunus presents this as a suspended report (mawquf), likely reflecting his own juristic reasoning (ijtihad) rather than a direct prophetic or imamic decree, a view that remains consistent with other established narrations on the subject.
